newsitem.title: USA: Conn. releases $2.5 mln bond for historic schooner.
newsitem.headline: Conn. releases $2.5 mln bond for historic schooner.

text.p: Connecticut has released a $2.5 million bond to build a recreation of the historic schooner "Amistad," officials at maritime museum Mystic Seaport said Tuesday.

They said the bond was released after Hartford-based Phoenix Home Life Mutual Insurance Co said it would contribute $100,000 to the project and guarantee that a total of $300,000 would be raised through the private sector.
The Phoenix contribution met the state's matching funds requirements for release of the bond, which was originally approved in 1994.
Interest in the ship has been revived by director Steven Spielberg's forthcoming movie, "Amistad," which tells the true story of 53 African slaves who seized the ship on its way to Cuba in 1839.
The mutineers were captured off the coast of Montauk, Long Island, brought to trial and eventually freed.
Spielberg recently spent several days at Mystic Seaport filming the movie.
The museum last year helped form Amistad America Inc., a non-profit group seeking funds for the recreation and operation of the vessel.
When completed, the schooner will be outfitted as a learning center and exhibit space, plying coastal waterways and rivers in the U.S.

The recreated "Amistad" is expected to earn about $300,000 per year in group fees, the museum said. It will be on display to the museum's visitors during construction, which is expected to begin this fall.
